name: MITRE ATT&CK 20.1
description: MITRE ATT&CK (Adversarial Tactics, Techniques and Common Knowledge) 20.1, MITRE's knowledge base of adversary behaviour and the detection of it (https://attack.mitre.org/). ATT&CK describes what adversaries do as a graph: tactics, the adversary's objectives; techniques and sub-techniques that achieve them; the groups, campaigns, malware and tools that use them; the mitigations that counter them; and, since version 20, detection strategies, analytics and data components. Generated from the official STIX 2.1 bundles of the Enterprise, Mobile and ICS domains published in mitre-attack/attack-stix-data at tag v20.1 (https://github.com/mitre-attack/attack-stix-data/tree/v20.1): each active object is a node, labelled by its category; each relationship object and embedded reference is a relationship between the categories of its ends. Revoked and deprecated objects are left out.

ATTACKObject.description: An object of the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base: a tactic, technique, mitigation, group, campaign, malware, tool, detection strategy, analytic, data component or asset. Every node carries this label, 5657 in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1; the label of its category, e.g. Technique, says what kind of object it is.

stixId.name: stixId
stixId.description: The STIX identifier of the ATT&CK object, e.g. `attack-pattern--0042a9f5-f053-4769-b3ef-9ad018dfa298`. Unique across the domains.

name.name: name
name.description: The ATT&CK name of the object, e.g. `Spearphishing Attachment`.

description.name: description
description.description: The ATT&CK description of the object, as plain text.

url.name: url
url.description: The URL of the object on attack.mitre.org, e.g. `https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001`.

created.name: created
created.description: When the ATT&CK object was created.

modified.name: modified
modified.description: When the ATT&CK object was last modified.

domains.name: domains
domains.description: The ATT&CK domains the object belongs to: Enterprise, Mobile or ICS.

version.name: version
version.description: The ATT&CK version of the object, e.g. `1.2`, as it has changed over releases.

Tactic.description: A tactic: the 'why' of an attack, the adversary's tactical objective, e.g. Stealth or Privilege Escalation. Techniques serve a tactic through the technique's kill chain phases. Holds 39 Tactic objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 15, Mobile 12, ICS 12. Examples: Initial Access, Execution, Persistence.

Technique.description: A technique: the 'how' of an attack, the means by which an adversary achieves a tactical objective. A sub-technique is a more specific technique, linked to its parent by SUBTECHNIQUE_OF. Holds 935 Technique objects in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. Examples: Activate Firmware Update Mode, Monitor Process State, Automated Collection.

Analytic_LOG_SOURCE_REF_DataComponent.description: A data component the log sources of an analytic collect, from its `x_mitre_log_source_references`. Links 5233 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 4190, Mobile 614, ICS 429. e.g. Analytic 0001 (AN0001) watches the data component Cloud Service Metadata (DC0070); Analytic 0002 (AN0002) watches the data component Network Connection Creation (DC0082); Analytic 0003 (AN0003) watches the data component Process Creation (DC0032).

Campaign_ATTRIBUTED_TO_Group.description: The campaign is attributed to the group it is attributed to. Links 27 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 26, ICS 5, Mobile 1. e.g. C0011 is attributed to Transparent Tribe; C0017 is attributed to APT41; Operation Dream Job is attributed to Lazarus Group.

Campaign_USES_Malware.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 96 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 92, ICS 6, Mobile 3. e.g. Night Dragon uses ASPXSpy; CostaRicto uses PS1; Operation Spalax uses njRAT.

Campaign_USES_Technique.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 1351 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1213, Mobile 44, ICS 94. e.g. Frankenstein uses Data from Local System; Night Dragon uses Security Account Manager; CostaRicto uses Data from Local System.

Campaign_USES_Tool.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 81 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 81. e.g. Frankenstein uses Empire; Night Dragon uses gsecdump; CostaRicto uses PsExec.

DetectionStrategy_ANALYTIC_REF_Analytic.description: The analyses a detection strategy holds, from its `x_mitre_analytic_refs`. Links 2271 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1758, Mobile 213, ICS 300. e.g. Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS) has Analytic 0001 (AN0001); Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for C2 has Analytic 0002 (AN0002); T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms has Analytic 0006 (AN0006).

DetectionStrategy_DETECTS_Technique.description: The detection strategy detects the technique it detects. Links 935 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 706, Mobile 125, ICS 104. e.g. Detect Access to Cloud Instance Metadata API (IaaS) detects Cloud Instance Metadata API; Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for C2 detects Publish/Subscribe Protocols; T1136.002 Detection Strategy - Domain Account Creation Across Platforms detects Domain Account.

Group_USES_Malware.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Group_USES_Technique.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Group_USES_Tool.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 475 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 475. e.g. Cleaver uses Mimikatz; Ke3chang uses Mimikatz; APT12 uses HTRAN.

Malware_USES_Technique.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Mitigation_MITIGATES_Technique.description: The mitigation prevents, or makes harder, the technique it mitigates. Links 2068 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 1477, Mobile 167, ICS 424. e.g. Authorization Enforcement mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode; Access Management mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode; Communication Authenticity mitigates Activate Firmware Update Mode.

Technique_KILL_CHAIN_PHASE_Tactic.description: The tactic a technique serves, from the `kill_chain_phases` of the technique. Links 1149 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 881, Mobile 145, ICS 123. e.g. Activate Firmware Update Mode serves the Inhibit Response Function tactic; Monitor Process State serves the Collection tactic; Automated Collection serves the Collection tactic.

Technique_SUBTECHNIQUE_OF_Technique.description: The technique is a sub-technique of the more general technique it is of. Links 552 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 479, Mobile 47, ICS 26. e.g. Download All is a sub-technique of Program Download; Online Edit is a sub-technique of Program Download; Program Append is a sub-technique of Program Download.

Technique_TARGETS_Asset.description: The technique targets the asset it targets. Links 933 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: ICS 933. e.g. Activate Firmware Update Mode targets Human-Machine Interface (HMI); Monitor Process State targets Human-Machine Interface (HMI); Automated Collection targets Programmable Logic Controller (PLC).

Tool_USES_Technique.description: The source uses the target in the course of an attack: a group or campaign uses a technique, malware or tool; malware or a tool uses a technique. Links 891 pairs in MITRE ATT&CK 20.1: Enterprise 869, Mobile 22. e.g. Mimikatz uses LSASS Memory; Windows Credential Editor uses LSASS Memory; pwdump uses Security Account Manager.
